problem_text:
A logistics center must design a procurement and storage strategy for a critical component across a 14-day operational window.  
The starting stock at the commencement of the planning interval is 9 units.  
In each day \( t = 1, \dots, 14 \), the vendor permits the center to issue a purchase request, the size of which must be no less than 10 and no more than 40 units.  
Nevertheless, every purchase request is subject to a 4-day transit delay before it becomes available for fulfilling requirements or rebuilding stock.  
The daily requirement for the component is specified as follows:  

* Day 1: 30 units  
* Day 2: 21 units  
* Day 3: 28 units  
* Day 4: 25 units  
* Day 5: 50 units  
* Day 6: 37 units  
* Day 7: 53 units  
* Day 8: 54 units  
* Day 9: 28 units  
* Day 10: 12 units  
* Day 11: 11 units  
* Day 12: 10 units  
* Day 13: 50 units  
* Day 14: 27 units  

Stockouts are tolerated, but any unfulfilled requirement is considered lost and will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the planning window, component quantities may be treated as continuous, and the total physical stock held at any moment must remain within the storage limit of 44 units.  

On the fourth day, the maximum permissible purchase quantity is 37 units.  
On the twelfth day, the physical stock on hand must be no lower than 33 units.  

The aggregate expenditure over the planning interval comprises three elements: the procurement expense, charged at 6 per unit purchased; the storage expense, charged at 2 per unit kept from one day to the next; and the shortage penalty, charged at 6 per unit of unmet requirement.  
Identify the optimal purchase quantity for each day and monitor the ensuing stock and shortage levels in order to minimize the total expenditure.
